memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Psoriasis, insomnia, and depression.
Evidence: Chronic plaque psoriasis on elbows and knees, reports difficulty initiating sleep, low mood, anhedonia.
Symptoms and examination: Well‑appearing, erythematous scaly plaques 2‑3 cm on extensor surfaces, no joint swelling; reports sleep latency ~45 min, daytime fatigue, PHQ‑9‑consistent low energy. Smoking status: never. No inhaler prescribed; technique not applicable.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
clobetasol 0.05% cream – apply BD to affected areas
calcipotriol ointment – apply OD to plaques
methotrexate 7.5 mg – take once weekly
folic acid 5 mg – take daily
melatonin 3 mg – take at HS
trazodone 50 mg – take at HS
sertraline 50 mg – take daily
escitalopram 10 mg – take daily
mirtazapine 15 mg – take at HS

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
LFT: ALT 28 U/L (7‑56), AST 24 U/L (10‑40), ALP 78 U/L (30‑120), GGT 22 U/L (0‑51), Bilirubin 0.9 mg/dL (0.2‑1.2).
CBC: Hb 13.2 g/dL (12‑16), WBC 6.5 ×10⁹/L (4‑10), Platelets 250 ×10⁹/L (150‑400).
Creatinine 0.8 mg/dL (0.6‑1.2).
TSH 2.1 µIU/mL (0.4‑4.0).
Vitamin B12 350 pg/mL (200‑900).
PHQ‑9 12 (0‑27).
Insomnia Severity Index 15 (0‑28).

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Psoriasis, insomnia, depression – stable on treatment.
Evidence: LFT shows mild ALT rise, patient notes improved sleep but residual itching.
Symptoms and examination: Plaques thinner, scaling mild on elbows/knees; sleep latency ~30 min, reports feeling more rested; mood better, occasional tearfulness, denies suicidal ideation. Smoking status: never. No inhaler; technique not applicable.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Psoriasis, insomnia, depression – improving.
Evidence: LFT normalized, PHQ‑9 down, ISI improved.
Symptoms and examination: Plaques faint pink, minimal scaling; sleep latency ~20 min, feels rested; mood stable, reports enjoying work, no guilt. Smoking status: never. No inhaler; technique not applicable.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Via clinic app: ‘Over past week my psoriasis plaques have flared up on my scalp and back, itchy and red. Work stress high, sleeping only 5‑6 hours, feeling down again.’

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Refer to Dermatology for refractory scalp psoriasis. Continue current methotrexate 5 mg weekly, folic acid, topical steroids. Request advice on possible biologic therapy.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Dermatology notes: Scalp psoriasis severe, recommend adding calcipotriol‑betamethasone combo BD scalp, continue methotrexate, consider etanercept if no improvement in 8 weeks. No contraindications.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Follow‑up appointment booked with Dr Suresh Menon (D05) for 2026-04-10 at 10:30 am. Reason: review psoriasis treatment and mental health.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Psoriasis, insomnia, depression – post‑dermatology advice.
Evidence: Scalp plaques erythematous, thick scale; back plaques moderate.
Symptoms and examination: Prescribed calcipotriol‑betamethasone BD scalp, continue clobetasol BD body, methotrexate 5 mg weekly unchanged. Sleep latency ~35 min, mood low‑moderate, PHQ‑9 11. Smoking status: never. Inhaler technique not applicable.
